newsitem.title: JAPAN: Shimizu leads drop in Japan construction shares.
newsitem.headline: Shimizu leads drop in Japan construction shares.

text.p: Shares of Japanese general contractors O#CON.T were weak in Tokyo on Wednesday because of lingering worries over their financial health, brokers said.

The sector's decliners were led by Shimizu Corp, whose shares slipped to their lowest level in over a decade. As of 0426 GMT, the shares stood 15 yen down at 704 yen after earlier dipping as low as 695 yen, below the low of 708 yen marked in December 1986. Turnover was 1.30 million.
Taisei Corp also dipped eight yen to 503 yen in a turnover of 998,000, while Obayashi Corp slipped nine yen to 734 in a turnover of 661,000.

"It is not as if new factors arose to depress the construction sector. The downward adjustment phase of the sector is a little behind that of banks and investors are hurrying to catch up," said a broker at a "Big Four" brokerage.

There are lingering worries about the financial health of Japan's general contractors in light of the hefty amount of debts they have guaranteed. Private research company Teikoku Databank last month estimated their debt guarantees totalled 3.22 trillion yen at the end of September 1996.
